title: Dead Air at Mirror Lake
background: At a lakeside lodge, the founders and staff of fledgling audio-tech company Echowire gather for an all-hands retreat. CEO Niall Quist is found dead at 9:31 p.m. inside the locked generator shed, apparently killed by a blow from a metal microphone stand.
key_evidence: The dining-room security camera has an unbroken, cryptographically signed recording showing Sera Venn seated beside the fireplace from 9:16 to 9:22 p.m. The murder weapon's impact analysis places the fatal blow at approximately 9:18 p.m., making it objectively impossible for Sera to have been at the generator shed at that time if the recording is genuine.

Sera Venn.motive: Niall planned to expose that she had secretly diverted company funds into an abandoned project and remove her from the company.

Mara Sol.motive: Niall intended to blame her for irregular accounts that she had falsified to conceal mounting debts.

Theo Brand.relationship_to_victim: A rival executive whose promotion Niall had blocked
Theo Brand.motive: Niall had discovered Theo was negotiating a lucrative deal behind the company's back.

Juniper Hale.relationship_to_victim: A former protégé who considered Niall her mentor
Juniper Hale.motive: Niall had stolen credit for her breakthrough audio algorithm and threatened to destroy her career if she challenged him.

timeline.Sera Venn: At 9:18 p.m., Sera was inside the generator shed, using a concealed duplicate of the microphone stand to kill Niall before returning to the lodge through the service tunnel.
timeline.Mara Sol: At 9:18 p.m., Mara was in the lodge office reviewing printed expense reports and making a phone call to the company's auditor.
timeline.Theo Brand: At 9:18 p.m., Theo was on the lakeside dock, recording a voice message for a prospective investor while watching the retreat's boat moored nearby.
timeline.Juniper Hale: At 9:18 p.m., Juniper was in the dining room kitchen assembling desserts with the lodge caretaker, who later confirmed her presence.

statements.Sera Venn: I was checking the generator shed's equipment at 9:18 p.m. That part of the evening remains vivid to me: the hum, the chill, and the sense of wanting to get back indoors.
statements.Mara Sol: At 9:18 p.m., I was in the lodge office reviewing printed expense reports while speaking by phone with the company's auditor. I was absorbed in reconciling the figures, with papers spread across the desk and the office quiet around me.
statements.Theo Brand: At 9:18 p.m., I was on the lakeside dock recording a voice message for a prospective investor while watching the retreat's boat. I was concentrating on choosing my words carefully, with the water and the empty shoreline beyond me.
statements.Juniper Hale: At 9:18 p.m., I was in the dining-room kitchen assembling desserts with the lodge caretaker, who can confirm I stayed there. I was focused on arranging the finishing touches, with the kitchen conversation and sweet smell filling the room.

title: Murder on the Midnight Current
background: The luxury riverboat Maribel is hosting a glittering fundraiser when its philanthropic founder, Orson Vale, is found dead in the locked chart room just after the vessel passes beneath the old railway bridge. A shattered champagne flute lies beside him, and the gala continues in confusion while the captain orders the ship held at the next quay.
key_evidence: The chart-room access log records Celia Voss's personal keycard opening the room at 9:52 p.m., while the fixed ballroom camera shows Celia continuously seated at the auction table from 9:49 to 9:56 p.m.; the camera's timestamp is independently synchronized with the ship's navigation system.

Celia Voss.role: The fundraiser's auctioneer and event producer
Celia Voss.motive: Orson planned to expose that Celia had diverted sponsorship money into a secret account.

Dr. Bram Ellery.role: A river ecologist and gala speaker
Dr. Bram Ellery.relationship_to_victim: A former research colleague whom Orson publicly discredited
Dr. Bram Ellery.motive: Orson's sabotage cost Bram a major grant and ruined his standing in the scientific community.

Nadia Quill.relationship_to_victim: Orson's niece and an employee of the foundation
Nadia Quill.motive: Orson had rewritten his will to remove Nadia from the family trust after discovering her gambling debts.

Felix Marr.role: A private antiques dealer and donor
Felix Marr.relationship_to_victim: Orson's longtime rival in riverfront property deals
Felix Marr.motive: Orson was about to cancel a lucrative sale after learning Felix had forged an artifact's provenance.

timeline.Celia Voss: At 9:52 p.m., Celia was actually in the chart room, having used a copied keycard to enter and strike Orson with the weighted base of a brass signal lamp before returning to the ballroom.
timeline.Dr. Bram Ellery: At 9:52 p.m., Bram was on the forward observation deck explaining river sediment to three guests and remained there until the ship cleared the railway bridge.
timeline.Nadia Quill: At 9:52 p.m., Nadia was in the galley counting replacement champagne bottles with the catering chief, whose inventory sheet bears her signature at 9:54 p.m.
timeline.Felix Marr: At 9:52 p.m., Felix was in the men's lavatory beside the ballroom, where a non-guest deckhand saw him washing blood from a small cut on his thumb.

statements.Celia Voss: At 9:52 p.m., my personal keycard was still in my handbag. I remained at the auction table, concentrating on the bidding and keeping the evening's schedule moving.
statements.Dr. Bram Ellery: At 9:52 p.m., I was on the forward observation deck explaining river sediment to three guests. I stayed there until the Maribel cleared the old railway bridge, with the river discussion continuing throughout.
statements.Nadia Quill: At 9:52 p.m., I was in the galley counting replacement champagne bottles with the catering chief. I signed the inventory sheet at 9:54 p.m. and then returned to the hospitality arrangements.
statements.Felix Marr: At 9:52 p.m., I was in the men's lavatory beside the ballroom, washing blood from a small cut on my thumb. A deckhand saw me there, and I went back toward the gala once the wound was clean.

title: The Bitter Morning
background: On the morning after the grand reopening of Hearth & Crumb, owner Mara Venn is found dead in the flour room, struck with a cast-iron bread mold. The bakery's ovens are still warm, but the front doors remain locked and the staff discover the body just before opening.
key_evidence: At 6:12 a.m., the neighboring pharmacy's exterior camera records Celia Rusk continuously inside the pharmacy's locked consultation room, making her claimed presence in the bakery at that moment impossible.

Celia Rusk.role: Head baker and Mara's former business partner
Celia Rusk.relationship_to_victim: Mara bought out Celia's share of the bakery six months earlier
Celia Rusk.motive: Celia believed Mara had cheated her and planned to replace her after the reopening

Jonas Pell.relationship_to_victim: Mara's principal flour and chocolate supplier
Jonas Pell.motive: Mara was about to expose Jonas for secretly substituting cheaper ingredients

Iris Venn.relationship_to_victim: Mara was Iris's guardian and employer
Iris Venn.motive: Mara had recently changed her will, cutting Iris out after discovering stolen cash

Theo March.motive: Mara had secured the lease on the town's only second storefront, blocking Theo's expansion

timeline.Celia Rusk: At 6:12 a.m., Celia was inside Hearth & Crumb's flour room after entering through the rear door at 6:08, and she killed Mara with the bread mold.
timeline.Jonas Pell: At 6:12 a.m., Jonas was unloading flour sacks at the town market two streets away, where the market clerk watched him sign the delivery ledger.
timeline.Iris Venn: At 6:12 a.m., Iris was at home speaking by telephone with the bakery's accountant about the previous day's receipts.
timeline.Theo March: At 6:12 a.m., Theo was opening his own shop on Mill Street, observed by his apprentice and the first morning customer.

statements.Celia Rusk: At 6:12 a.m., I was in the flour room finishing the morning preparation. The reopening had left me determined to prove that my work still belonged at Hearth & Crumb.
statements.Jonas Pell: At 6:12 a.m., I was unloading flour sacks at the town market, with the market clerk watching me sign the delivery ledger. Mara’s accusations had made the bakery’s supply business tense, but I went there to complete the delivery as promised.
statements.Iris Venn: At 6:12 a.m., I was at home speaking by telephone with the bakery’s accountant about the previous day’s receipts. Mara’s changes to her will had hurt me deeply, but I still hoped to explain the missing cash and repair our relationship.
statements.Theo March: At 6:12 a.m., I was opening my shop on Mill Street, observed by my apprentice and the first customer of the morning. Mara’s new lease had blocked my expansion, but I intended to compete with Hearth & Crumb rather than abandon my own business.

title: The Bitter Morning
background: Mara Venn, owner of Hearth & Hallow Bakery, was found dead in the cooling room shortly after dawn, the morning after her lavish grand reopening. A display tray had been smashed beside her, and a smear of raspberry filling marked the floor leading toward the rear delivery door.
key_evidence: A timestamped security camera at the neighboring pharmacy shows the bakery's rear delivery door remained fully closed from 5:00 to 5:25 a.m., so it could not have been used as an entrance or exit during that period.

Liora Pell.relationship_to_victim: Mara's longtime employee and former business partner
Liora Pell.motive: Mara had secretly planned to replace Liora after discovering she had been selling the bakery's recipes to a rival shop.

Jonas Venn.role: Mara's younger brother and delivery driver
Jonas Venn.relationship_to_victim: Sibling and co-owner of the bakery building
Jonas Venn.motive: Mara intended to sell the building, leaving Jonas without his expected inheritance or job.

Priya Dastur.relationship_to_victim: Business neighbor whose café supplied Hearth & Hallow
Priya Dastur.motive: Mara had threatened to end their supply contract after Priya publicly criticized the reopening's expensive renovations.

Calder Wren.relationship_to_victim: Former friend and invited guest at the reopening
Calder Wren.motive: Mara possessed evidence that Calder had fabricated several of his celebrated restaurant reviews.

timeline.Liora Pell: At 5:12 a.m., Liora entered through the rear delivery door, struck Mara in the cooling room with a dough scraper, and left the scraper beside the broken display tray.
timeline.Jonas Venn: At 5:12 a.m., Jonas was in his van at the town fuel station, filling the tank before beginning the bakery's morning deliveries.
timeline.Priya Dastur: At 5:12 a.m., Priya was in her café across the alley, calibrating the espresso grinder while her opening employee watched.
timeline.Calder Wren: At 5:12 a.m., Calder was in the upstairs apartment above the bakery, asleep after returning from the reopening party.

statements.Liora Pell: At 5:12 a.m., I entered through the rear delivery door before going to the cooling room to begin the bakery's early preparations. I expected the quiet morning to follow its usual routine, with the display area ready for the day's first customers.
statements.Jonas Venn: At 5:12 a.m., I was at the town fuel station filling my van before starting the bakery's morning deliveries. The attendant saw me there, and I had not yet reached the bakery when the day's work was supposed to begin.
statements.Priya Dastur: At 5:12 a.m., I was across the alley in my café, calibrating the espresso grinder while my opening employee watched. I was preparing our first service and had not crossed into the bakery during that early part of the morning.
statements.Calder Wren: At 5:12 a.m., I was asleep in the upstairs apartment above the bakery after returning from Mara's reopening party. I had gone upstairs expecting to rest until later, and I did not begin the morning near the bakery's work areas.

title: The Empty Applause
background: At the opening night of the Vesper House Gallery, a shattered skylight and a missing painting suggest a break-in amid the crowded celebration. Gallery director Mara Venn is found dead at 9:21 p.m. in the locked archive office, struck with a bronze sculpture from the missing exhibit. An uninvolved volunteer discovers the body after the gallery lights return.
key_evidence: The gallery's unedited opening livestream is time-synchronized to the city clock and shows Iris Bell continuously speaking at the main podium at exactly 9:12 p.m.; the coroner places Mara's fatal blow at 9:12 p.m.

Niko Vale.motive: Mara had discovered that Niko was concealing costly insurance discrepancies.

Elsa Quill.motive: Mara planned to publicly discredit Elsa's restoration methods and end her career.

Tomas Reed.motive: Mara was about to report Tomas for selling temporary access codes to art thieves.

Iris Bell.motive: Mara had learned Iris forged the signature on her celebrated series and intended to cancel the exhibition.

timeline.Niko Vale: At 9:12 p.m., Niko was in the loading dock office replacing a mislabeled inventory tag on a shipping crate.
timeline.Elsa Quill: At 9:12 p.m., Elsa was in the sculpture room photographing a damaged pedestal for the gallery's insurance file.
timeline.Tomas Reed: At 9:12 p.m., Tomas was in the east gallery resetting a tripped motion sensor beside the skylight display.
timeline.Iris Bell: At 9:12 p.m., Iris was in the archive office striking Mara with the bronze sculpture and staging the broken-skylight burglary.

statements.Niko Vale: Mara’s insurance questions had put me under pressure, but I was still trying to keep the opening organized and running smoothly. At 9:12 p.m., I was in the loading dock office replacing a mislabeled inventory tag on a shipping crate.
statements.Elsa Quill: Mara’s plans to discredit my restoration work made the evening painful, but I wanted the gallery’s exhibition protected from further damage. At 9:12 p.m., I was in the sculpture room photographing a damaged pedestal for the insurance file.
statements.Tomas Reed: Mara’s threat to report my access-code dealings endangered my contract, yet I remained responsible for keeping the crowded gallery secure. At 9:12 p.m., I was in the east gallery resetting a tripped motion sensor beside the skylight display.
statements.Iris Bell: I kept my attention on the exhibition and hoped the opening would proceed without another dispute with Mara. At 9:12 p.m., I was in the archive office with her.
